description: Democratizing electricity distribution network analysis is a software platform described in the paper "Democratizing electricity distribution network analysis" in Data-Centric Engineering (Cambridge University Press, 2023), produced by Myriam Neaimeh, Matthew Deakin, Ryan Jenkinson and colleagues. The uptake of electric vehicles (EVs) and renewable energy technologies is changing the magnitude, variability, and direction of power flows in electricity networks. To ensure a successful transition to a net zero energy system, it will be necessary for a wide range of stakeholders to understand the impacts of these changing flows on networks. Coverage: Great Britain electricity distribution networks. Access is through the paper, which is available online; the paper describes the tool and its use cases, and no separate code link was verified, so the paper is the only link. Licence: not stated (data set page not reachable on 2026-10-01; the paper is CC-BY-4.0). Cost: no charge is stated in the metadata read; the paper's own access terms were not checked. Caveats: written from the paper's abstract and metadata only, so contents, quality and current availability are unchecked and the description may lag the source. It can support assessing congestion in electricity distribution networks from electric vehicles and low-carbon technologies. Related: the paper is the Data-Centric Engineering article 10.1017/dce.2022.41.
